b1-adj-stumm: Your friend was born without being able to speak, so he talks to everybody with his hands and signs. How do we describe him?
A film from 1920 has no sound at all. The actors only move their lips and you read the words on the screen. What kind of film is this?
You ask your sister a question, but she looks at you and does not say one single word. She just stays quiet.
b1-n-kompromiss: You want pizza and your friend wants sushi, so you both agree on pasta. Each of you gave up a little. What do we call this kind of solution?
Two colleagues want the same holiday week. After a long talk, each takes a few days less than they wanted and the problem is solved.
Your parents want you home at 10, you want to stay out until midnight. You agree on 11 o'clock and everybody is fairly happy.
b1-v-zusammenfassen: Your teacher gives you a ten-page text and asks you to write only the main points in five lines.
Your boss says: 'I do not have time to read the whole report. Please give me the short version in two sentences.'
You have three small files and want to put them all together into one single file.
b1-n-salon: You walk into a fancy shop where women get their hair cut, coloured and styled. What do you call this kind of place?
In an old, elegant house, guests sit in a large, beautiful room to talk and drink tea. It is the formal room for receiving visitors.
You want a manicure and a new hairstyle. Which word do you use for a 'beauty salon'?
b1-n-freiheit: After ten years in prison, a man walks through the gate. Now he can go wherever he wants again. What has he got back?
Teenagers want to decide for themselves when to go out and what to wear. They ask their parents for more of this.
In New York you see a huge green statue holding a torch. It stands for 'liberty'. Which word means this?
b1-adj-wahnsinnig: Your friend wants to cycle across the whole country in two days. You shake your head and say he is completely out of his mind.
The concert was unbelievably good, much better than anything you had ever seen. Which word means 'incredible' or 'crazy' here?
This morning the traffic was a massive mess, far more than anyone had ever seen. You describe it with one strong adjective.
b1-n-geschmack: You eat a piece of cake. It is sweet with a little lemon. What do you notice on your tongue?
Two friends choose very different clothes and furniture. One says: 'We simply have a different sense of what looks nice.' Which noun?
A guest asks if you want vanilla or strawberry ice cream. Which word means the 'flavour' of the ice cream?
b1-v-unterrichten: Every morning you stand in front of twenty pupils and explain maths to them. That is your job.
Your neighbour's son is bad at English, so you go to his house every Monday and give him lessons.
You work at a school and give lessons to children about history. Which verb means 'to teach'?
b1-n-urteil: In a court, the judge reads out the final decision at the end of the trial: guilty or not guilty. What is this decision called?
You see a new person for only ten seconds and decide he is rude. You formed an opinion about him far too quickly.
The trial is over. Everybody in the courtroom stands up to hear the verdict. Which noun do you need?
b1-n-gebaeude: You look at the city and see a very tall structure with many floors and offices. What is a structure with walls and a roof called?
The tourist guide says: 'The old town hall is a historic one from 1450.' Which noun means a house, church or tower in general?
Where is the post office? 'It is in that big grey one next to the church.' What do you call such a large structure?
b1-v-unterlassen: A sign at the hospital asks visitors not to make phone calls. It is a polite request: please do not do it.
The judge tells a man to stop insulting his neighbour and never to do it again. He must refrain from doing it.
You were supposed to turn off the oven, but you simply did not do it. Which verb means 'to fail to do' something you should do?
b1-n-flur: You enter your flat and take off your shoes in the narrow space between the front door and the other rooms.
At school, there is a long space between the classrooms where pupils walk and hang their jackets.
In a hotel you walk along a long, carpeted way with doors on both sides to find Room 214.
b1-adj-zweifach: You need your form in two identical copies. The office says it must be handed in in this way: two times.
The champion won the world title two times. People call him a champion of this kind.
A bag is sewn with two layers of material on every seam for extra strength. The protection is of this type.
b1-adv-halt: Your friend asks why the bus is always late. You shrug: 'It is what it is, that is just how things are.' Which small word expresses this feeling?
A child asks why the sky is blue. You do not know and answer in a relaxed way that it is simply like that.
Your colleague worries about a small mistake. You calm him: 'It happens, you just made an error.' Which little particle adds the 'simply' feeling?
b1-n-tabelle: In your spreadsheet you arrange numbers in rows and columns. What do you call this arrangement?
On Saturday evening you check the list of football teams with their points and positions. Your team is at the top of it.
In the maths book, you see a grid with columns for name, age and city. What is it?
b1-n-lieferung: You ordered a sofa online. A van brings it to your door on Thursday. What is this called?
A supermarket manager waits for the truck that brings fresh vegetables every morning. What noun describes what the truck brings?
The pizza shop says: 'Your order will arrive at your home in thirty minutes.' Which noun means 'delivery'?
b1-v-anzeigen: Someone stole your bike. You go to the police to officially tell them about the crime.
Your phone's screen shows the time and the date. Which verb describes what a screen or a board does with information?
The speedometer in a car points to 80 km/h. It shows the speed to the driver.
b1-n-fundbuero: You left your umbrella on the train. Where do you ask at the station if somebody found it?
At the airport you lost your wallet. You go to a special desk where found items are kept.
A child finds a mobile phone on the street and takes it to the place where lost things are collected.
b1-n-konflikt: Two neighbours argue for months about a fence and no longer talk to each other. Their disagreement is serious.
At work, two team members have opposite goals and keep clashing. The manager must solve the problem between them.
Your parents want you to study law, but you want to become an artist. This clash of wishes is a real problem.
b1-adj-offenbar: The lights are off and nobody answers the door. It seems clear that no one is at home. Which word means 'obviously'?
Your colleague has red eyes and yawns all day. It is clear that he did not sleep well.
The shop is dark and there is a sign on the door. You say: 'Apparently, they are closed today.'
b1-v-loben: Your child gets a great grade, and you tell her how proud you are and what a good job she did.
A boss says in a meeting: 'Excellent work, everyone!' What does he do to the team?
At a restaurant, you tell the cook that the soup was wonderful.
b1-n-klingel: You stand at your friend's front door and push the small button. A sound rings inside.
A bike has a little metal thing on the handlebar that you ring to warn pedestrians.
At the entrance there is a button next to the family names. You push it to let people inside know you are there.
b1-n-druck: Your tyre is flat. At the petrol station you check the number in bar. What do you measure?
Before an important exam you feel stressed because everybody expects a lot from you. You feel a lot of this.
The newspaper says the book is going to the factory where ink is put on paper. What is this process called?
b1-v-angeben: On the online form you must write your address and phone number, as asked.
At customs, the officer asks what goods you have. You tell him: 'Two bottles of wine.' You declare them.
A boy keeps bragging about his new car and expensive watch so that everybody looks at him.
b1-n-stufe: You walk up to the entrance. There are five stone ones to climb before you reach the door.
In a language course, you move from beginner to the next one: A2. What do we call such a stage?
Be careful at the bottom of the stairs, there is one small raised edge. Do not trip over it.
b1-adj-westlich: On a compass, the sun goes down in this direction. Which adjective describes it?
The town lies on the side of the river where the sun goes down. It is in the ___ part of the country.
A weather report says strong winds are coming from the direction where the sun sets.
b1-n-stern: At night in the countryside, you look up and see many small shining lights in the sky.
A teacher puts a shiny sticker with five points on your good homework.
A hotel has five of these on its sign. It is a luxury hotel.
b1-n-festplatte: Your computer stores all your photos and files inside this part. It is full and you need a bigger one.
You buy a small black box, connect it with a USB cable and copy all your files onto it as a backup.
The technician says that the part inside your laptop which stores data permanently is broken.
b1-v-reduzieren: You want to use less plastic, so you buy fewer plastic bags every month.
The shop cuts all prices by thirty percent in the summer sale.
Your doctor says you should eat less sugar and use less salt.
b1-adv-insgesamt: At the till, the cashier adds up all the items: 'That is 45 euros for everything together.' Which adverb means 'in total'?
Five guests came on Friday and three on Saturday. Counting both days, eight people came.
Looking at the whole year and not at single months, sales went up a bit. It was a good year.
b1-n-zuschauer: A man sits in the stadium and watches the football match with 50,000 other people.
You stand on the street and watch a street show without taking part. What are you?
One man at home watches a quiz show on TV and shouts the answers at the screen.
b1-n-misserfolg: A company launches a new product, but nobody buys it and they lose money. The launch was a total disaster.
You studied hard for the driving test but still failed. It is a disappointment, the opposite of success.
The film cost millions, but the cinemas were empty. The critics call it a big flop.
b1-adj-illegal: Downloading films from a pirate website breaks the law. What adjective describes this?
Driving a car without a licence is forbidden by law. Police say it is against the law.
Selling things on the street without any permit is not allowed. Which word means 'not legal'?
b1-v-einstellen: Your seat in the car is too far back. You move it so it fits your legs.
A restaurant needs a new waiter and gives a young man a job. The owner takes him on.
The bus company stops the night route because too few people use it.
b1-n-zertifikat: After finishing the language course, you receive an official paper that proves your level, B1.
At work, you complete a first-aid course and get an official paper to show your future boss.
You pass a swimming test and receive a paper that confirms your skills.
b1-n-station: The tram stops here. You wait with other people under a small roof with a sign showing the name of the place.
A voice on the train says: 'The next one is Alexanderplatz.' You need to get off there.
You ride the underground and count how many stops there are before you get off.
b1-n-zuhoerer: On the radio, a man calls the show and says he has been a regular fan of the programme for years and always tunes in.
A speaker at a conference says: 'Dear ladies and gentlemen,' to the people in the room who are paying attention. Which plural noun means these people?
A friend tells you a long story. You sit quietly and pay attention. You are a good one, a man who listens.
b1-v-zweifeln: Your friend says he will quit smoking, but you are not sure he really will. You do not believe it completely.
You are not sure the story is true, so you ask for proof.
Before the exam you think: 'Can I really do this?' You have no confidence in yourself.
b1-adj-durstig: After a long run in the sun, you want a big glass of water.
Your child says: 'Mum, can I have some juice? My throat is dry.'
At a hot summer picnic, everybody drinks a lot because they all need something to drink.
b1-n-verabredung: You and a friend agreed to meet at 7 in front of the cinema. What do you call this arrangement to meet?
A woman tells her boss she cannot stay late tonight because she has a romantic evening with someone.
In your calendar you write: 'Friday 3 p.m.: coffee with Anna.' It is a private meeting arranged earlier, not a doctor's visit.
b1-n-krise: A company has almost no money left and may have to close. Everybody is worried. It is a serious, difficult time.
At 45, a man doubts his job, his marriage and his whole life. People say he is in a mid-life one.
The news talks about a time of big economic trouble where many people lose their jobs.
b1-v-vertreten: Your teacher is ill, so another teacher takes her place and teaches her class today.
A lawyer speaks in court on behalf of her client.
Each class chooses one pupil to speak for them in the school council.
b1-n-geldautomat: You need cash on Sunday. You put your bank card into a machine in the wall and enter your PIN.
A tourist asks: 'Where can I take out money? Is there a machine nearby?'
Outside the bank there is a long queue of people waiting to get banknotes from a machine.
b1-n-grafik: In a presentation, one slide shows a pie chart and arrows instead of text.
A designer prepares pictures, icons and shapes for a website. What do we call such a picture?
The report has a picture with coloured bars that show the sales for each month.
b1-adj-populaer: Everybody at school knows him and wants to be his friend.
This song plays on the radio all day and everybody sings it. It is very well liked.
A restaurant has a queue outside every night because so many people love it.
b1-v-verhindern: You lock the door so thieves cannot get in. You want to make sure it does not happen.
A fence at the road keeps children from running into traffic. It stops an accident from happening.
The driver reacted fast and stopped the crash before it could happen.
b1-adv-dagegen: Everybody wants to start the meeting at 8, but you do not like the idea. Which small word means 'against it'?
The first car is cheap but slow. The second is fast but expensive. Which adverb means 'in contrast' when you compare them?
A friend asks: 'Do you mind if I open the window?' You say you have nothing against it. Which adverb means 'against it'?
b1-n-kommentar: Under a video on the internet, people write their opinions. What is one of these texts called?
During a football match on TV, a man speaks and explains what is happening in the game.
Your teacher writes a short note next to your essay, saying what you could improve.
b1-n-lehrling: A 16-year-old boy starts at a baker's workshop. He learns the job for three years and gets a small salary.
At a car garage, a young man learns the job by working next to the mechanics.
At the hairdresser's, a young man who is still learning the profession sweeps the floor and washes hair.
b1-n-tradition: Every Christmas your family cooks the same dish, just as your grandparents and their parents did before.
In some villages people wear special clothes for a festival that they have celebrated for hundreds of years.
Your new colleague asks why everybody brings cake on their birthday. You answer that it is a custom that has always been done.
b1-v-enthalten: You read the back of the cereal box. It has sugar and nuts in it, listed as ingredients.
At the hotel, the price already has breakfast in it. Nothing extra to pay.
The envelope has a letter and a photo inside.
b1-n-tanz: At a wedding, couples move to the music in the middle of the floor.
A friend invites you to a class where you learn waltz and tango steps.
At the club, a man smiles and asks: 'May I have this one with you?'
b1-adj-oeffentlich: The park, the library and the swimming pool are open for everybody and do not belong to one person.
The mayor holds a meeting in the town hall and everybody is allowed to come.
Smoking is forbidden in places like train stations, where everyone can go.
b1-n-umweltverschmutzung: Dirty smoke from factories and cars makes the air bad, and fish die in the river.
You walk along the beach and see plastic bottles and bags everywhere, and oil in the water.
A news report says that cities with many cars have grey, unhealthy air.
b1-v-korrigieren: Your teacher reads your homework and marks the mistakes in red pen.
You notice a typing error in your email and change it before sending.
You say a sentence with a wrong form and your friend gently tells you the right one.
b1-n-sonderpreis: A shop sign says: 'This week only: jackets for 20 euros instead of 50.'
A hotel offers a cheaper rate for guests who stay in January.
The cashier says: 'This is a limited offer, much lower than the usual price.'
b1-n-sorge: Your son is late and does not answer his phone. You feel a heavy, anxious feeling.
The doctor says: 'You have no reason to be anxious, everything is fine.' Which noun means this feeling?
A friend says: 'My exam is my biggest one right now.' It is something that troubles his mind.
b1-adj-komplett: You buy a puzzle and open the box. All 1000 pieces are there and none is missing.
The whole team came to the party, every single person.
A teacher says: 'Please read the whole text, not only the first page.'
b1-n-teilzeit: A mother works only four hours a day so she can pick up her children from school.
A student has a job in a cafe for 15 hours a week, between lectures.
At the job interview you are asked: 'Do you want to work full days or fewer hours?'
b1-v-behandeln: A doctor gives a patient medicine and care for his illness.
A teacher in class talks about a topic: today they cover climate change.
A good boss should act fairly and politely with all the employees.
b1-n-schlaf: At night you close your eyes in your bed and rest for eight hours. What do you get?
You yawn and say you need more of it because you feel tired all day.
A baby is calm and does not move. You whisper: 'Do not wake her, she is in a deep one.'
b1-n-modul: At university, a course is split into small parts, each with its own exam and credits.
A technician replaces one small unit of the machine which snaps in and out.
In your online training you finish the first of five parts and get a mark for it.
b1-adv-danach: First you eat dinner. After that, you wash the dishes. Which adverb means 'after it'?
We see a film first, and then we can go for a drink.
A teacher says: 'First the exam, and what comes next?' Which word do you use for 'afterwards'?
b1-v-ankuendigen: At the station, a voice says that the train will arrive late.
A singer tells her fans on social media that a new album comes out in May.
Your boss tells everybody in advance that there will be a meeting on Monday.
b1-n-blitz: During a storm, the sky suddenly lights up bright white, followed by a loud bang.
Tourists take photos in a dark church and the little light of the camera goes off.
On the road, a speed camera takes a picture of your car with a bright light.
b1-adj-einsam: An old man lives alone, has no friends nearby and nobody visits him. He feels sad.
You move to a new city and know nobody. On Saturday evening you sit alone at home.
A small house stands far away from any village at the end of a quiet road.
b1-n-beschreibung: The police ask a witness to tell them what the thief looked like.
Your teacher says: 'Write a text about your best friend: face, hair, character.'
The website tells you about the size, colour and features of the product.
b1-v-heizen: It is winter and very cold, so you turn on the radiators.
In the countryside, grandpa puts wood in the stove to make the room warm.
Your flat is freezing, so you warm up the rooms.
b1-n-aenderung: You booked a flight, but you need another date. You call the airline to ask for a switch.
A teacher announces the new time for the test: a different room and different hour.
You edit a text and the program marks everything that is new in it.
b1-n-ofen: To bake bread and cakes, you put them in a hot box in the kitchen.
In the pizzeria, the cook puts the pizza into a large, stone, wood-fired one.
In an old farmhouse, a tiled one warms the living room in winter.
b1-n-eisenbahn: A hobbyist has small tracks and tiny locomotives in his basement. It is a model one.
In the 1800s, a new transport with steam engines and tracks connected the cities.
A boy loves to watch long lines of carriages roll along the tracks.
b1-adj-folgend: The email says: 'Please bring these things', followed by a list. Which adjective means 'what comes next'?
The teacher says: 'Please answer the questions below.' Which adjective describes what comes after?
The manager says: 'Note the points below: first, second, third.' Which adjective fits?
b1-v-auffallen: You wear a bright red coat in a crowd of grey ones. Everybody notices you.
A mistake in the text was so big that it caught the teacher's eye at once.
A very tall man walks into a small village shop and everybody looks at him.
b1-n-export: A factory sends cars to customers in other countries.
A country sells many goods abroad. It is the opposite of import.
Your uncle's company sells wine to shops in Japan.
b1-n-strecke: How far do you have to drive today from Berlin to Munich by car? You ask about the length of the way.
On the train map, you check the line between two cities.
A runner prepares for a race of 10 km and checks the course.
b1-v-abbiegen: You drive, and the navigation says: 'At the next corner, go left.'
Tell the taxi driver: 'Please take the next street to the right.'
A cyclist shows with his arm that he will go right at the crossing.
b1-n-verstaendnis: You were late because of a broken train. Your boss says he can see why and is not angry. He shows this.
In the English test, there is a part where you read a text and answer questions to show you got the meaning. It is a reading skill.
A friend is upset, and you listen carefully and show that you feel what he feels.
b1-adj-eindeutig: The referee watched the video: the ball was out, no doubt.
The instructions are so clear that nobody can read them in two ways.
The test result leaves no room for doubt.
b1-n-sieger: After the race, a man stands on the top step and receives the gold medal.
In a chess tournament, the man who won the most games gets the cup.
The quiz is over, and the host announces which man got the most points.
b1-adv-urspruenglich: The house was first a farm, but now it is a hotel. At the beginning it was a farm.
I wanted to study medicine at first, but later I changed my mind.
Which adverb means 'at the beginning, before things changed'?
b1-n-einzelheit: The witness tells the police every small piece of information about what happened.
A boss says: 'I do not want just the outline. I want every small point.'
In the contract you read the fine points: dates, prices and conditions.
b1-v-erhoehen: The landlord makes the rent higher from January.
You turn the music up to make it louder.
A trainer wants to make the speed higher for the runners every week.
b1-n-ufer: You sit by the river and eat a sandwich at the edge of the water.
A swimmer reaches the land at the edge of the lake.
Two towns lie on opposite sides of a river. You need a bridge to get from one side to the other.
b1-n-studio: A singer records her new album in a room with microphones and soundproof walls.
A TV host sits in a large room with cameras and bright lights.
A photographer invites you to a room with backdrops and lamps to take portraits.
b1-adj-gewohnt: You always sit on the same seat on the bus and take the same route. It is your normal routine.
After moving abroad, you are finally accustomed to the cold weather.
A waiter brings your coffee the same way as every day.
b1-v-unterstreichen: Your teacher says to draw a line under the important words in the text with a ruler.
The speaker raises his voice and points to the slide to make a point stand out.
With a yellow marker you mark the key sentences.
b1-n-entfernung: How far is it from your house to the airport? It is 30 km.
A sign shows: 'Berlin 250 km.' What noun means how far away a place is?
From the mountain, the town looks tiny because it is so far away.
b1-n-traene: When you chop onions, water runs down your cheeks.
At a sad film, a woman cries and a drop rolls over her cheek.
At a happy wedding, the bride's eye is wet and one drop falls.
b1-v-zelten: On holiday you sleep in a small cloth house in a field next to a river.
Friends go to the forest with sleeping bags and make a fire.
A campsite sign says: 'Here you can pitch your tent.' What verb describes what you do?
b1-n-zustand: You buy a used car and ask how it is: scratches, engine and tyres.
The doctor says the patient's health is stable right now.
The flat was returned in a clean and perfect way. What noun describes how something is?
b1-adj-senkrecht: A line on the whiteboard goes straight up from top to bottom, not sideways.
A flagpole stands straight up at a right angle to the ground.
On a plane, the back of the seat must be straight up before takeoff.
b1-n-chance: A company offers you a job abroad. It might not come again.
In football, a player has the ball in front of the goal. It is a great opportunity to score.
Your friend failed the first test. You say: 'Do not give up, you will get another try.'
b1-n-leser: A man loves books and reads two every week.
A man buys the daily paper every morning and reads it on the train.
A man writes a letter to the editor as someone who regularly buys and reads the newspaper.
b1-v-kaempfen: Two judo athletes compete for the gold medal.
A patient does not give up and keeps trying hard against his illness.
She works hard for years to get a scholarship.
b1-n-hitze: In July it is 38 degrees. Everybody is sweating and looks for shade.
You open the oven and strong warm air hits your face.
A weather report warns: 'Drink a lot and avoid the sun,' because it is very hot.
b1-adv-hinterher: Before the meeting nobody said anything, but later, after it, everybody had complaints. Which adverb means 'afterwards'?
First we work, and after that we celebrate.
You watch the film and eat popcorn first, and talk about it later.
b1-n-saison: Summer is the time for ice cream shops, winter for ski resorts. Business is busiest at a certain time of year.
In football, the games from August to May are all part of one of these.
Strawberries are cheap only in June, because it is their time of year.
b1-adj-bestimmt: You ask the waiter for one particular wine, the 2018 red, not just any wine.
A teacher says: 'Only students with a certain level may join this class.'
A friend says: 'I am looking for a specific book, but I cannot remember its name.'
b1-v-ueberqueren: You wait at the red light and then walk to the other side of the road.
A hiker goes over the bridge to the other side of the river.
A ship travels over the ocean to America.
b1-n-beginn: The film starts at 8. 'Please be there before the very first minute.' Which noun means the start?
A teacher says: 'At the opening of the lesson, we will do a short quiz.'
In the first minute of the match, a team scores a goal.
